mainTopic: Acquiring for a נכרי, רבית when a נכרי converts, fining a lender for a שטר with רבית, early-dated documents, and money paid for a void sale
overview: The amud opens by finishing an argument that a Jew should be able to acquire for a נכרי, just as a קטן can acquire by rabbinic law. The גמרא rejects this comparison: a Jewish קטן will one day be eligible for שליחות, but a נכרי never will. Next, a ברייתא teaches that when a loan with רבית involves a נכרי who converts, the outcome depends on whether the interest was folded into the principal before or after the conversion. רבי יוסי says a convert borrower always pays the רבית, and the הלכה follows him. רבא explains the reason: so people will not say he converted to escape his debt. Then a ברייתא records a dispute about a שטר with רבית written in it: רבי מאיר fines the lender even the קרן, while the חכמים do not. This dispute is used to explain why early-dated loan documents are invalid, and ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן give two different reasons. Finally, a story about a mortgaged orchard raises a question: when a sale is void, is the buyer's money collected like a loan with a שטר or like an oral loan? אביי links this question to a statement of רבי אסי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A minor can acquire by rabbinic law, so a gentile should too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its comparison: a קטן has זכיה מדרבנן even without שליחות, so the same should apply to a נכרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A minor still has the power to acquire by rabbinic law. Here too it should be no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an argument that began before this section. Just as a קטן can acquire through another person by rabbinic law, a Jew should be able to acquire on behalf of a נכרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem being discussed is that there is no שליחות for a נכרי, so a Jew should not be able to acquire for him. The argument answers this with the case of a קטן: a קטן is also not part of שליחות, yet the רבנן still gave him the power of זכיה. So lacking שליחות should not block זכיה for a נכרי either.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquiring something, here through another person acting on one's behalf
By rabbinic law, not from the Torah itself
Here too it is no different, a formula used to compare two cases

phrases.english: he has the power to acquire by rabbinic law.
Here too, it is no different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an argument that began before this section
steps.raayaObject: That a Jew can acquire on behalf of a נכרי even though there is no שליחות for a נכרי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rabbinic law that a קטן, who has no שליחות, can still acquire through someone else

steps.title: Rejecting the comparison: a minor will grow up, a gentile will not
steps.stepSummary: The comparison fails because a Jewish קטן will eventually be part of שליחות, while a נכרי never will.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. A Jew will eventually reach the stage where agency applies to him. A gentile will never reach that stage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the comparison from Step 1 and shows that a קטן and a נכרי are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jewish קטן is only temporarily outside of שליחות, because one day he will be an adult. That is why the רבנן were willing to give him זכיה early. A נכרי is permanently outside of שליחות, so the רבנן never set up זכיה for him through a Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so, the גמרא's own rejection of the previous argument
Agency, having someone act on your behalf
Will come into the category of, will eventually become eligible

steps.whatToRemember: A קטן's lack of שליחות is temporary, but a נכרי's is permanent. So the rabbinic זכיה given to a קטן does not carry over to a נכרי.

phrases.english: But it is not so:
a Jew will come into the category of agency,
phrases.notes: He means the Jewish minor, who will become eligible once he grows up.

phrases.english: a gentile will not come into the category of agency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in Step 1
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between a קטן and a נכרי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A קטן will eventually be eligible for שליחות, but a נכרי never will, so the two cases are not alike

steps.title: A Jew borrowed with interest from a gentile who later converted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if the נכרי lender folded the רבית into the principal before he converted, he collects everything. If he did it after converting, he collects only the קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A Jew borrowed money from a gentile with interest. The gentile added the interest onto the loan as part of the debt, and then he converted. If he added it to the loan before he converted, he collects the principal and also the interest. If he added it to the loan after he converted, he collects the principal but not the interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about a loan with רבית where the נכרי lender becomes a גר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on when the interest was folded into the principal (זקפן במלוה). If this happened while the lender was still a נכרי, the interest became part of a regular debt before he converted, so he may collect all of it. If he folded it in only after converting, it was still interest when he became a Jew, and a Jew may not collect רבית from a Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: Interest on a loan, forbidden between Jews
He set the interest against him as a loan, meaning he combined it into the principal as one debt
He converted and became a גר
The principal, the original amount lent
Collects payment

steps.confusionAlert: Converting alone does not decide the outcome. What matters is whether the interest had already been folded into the principal before the conversion.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלָּוָה מָעוֹת מִן הַנׇּכְרִי בְּרִבִּית,
phrases.english: A Jew who borrowed money from a gentile with interest,
and he set it against him as a loan, and he converted.
phrases.notes: "He" is the gentile lender. He rolled the interest into the principal, and then he himself converted.

phrases.english: If before he converted
he set it against him as a loan,

phrases.english: he collects the principal and he collects the interest.
But if after he converted
he set it against him as a loan,

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹבֶה אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וְאֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה אֶת הָרִבִּית.
phrases.english: he collects the principal but does not collect the interest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic with a ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נכרי lender who folded the רבית into the principal before converting collects both the principal and the interest. If he did so after converting, he collects only the principal.

steps.title: A gentile borrowed with interest from a Jew and later converted
steps.stepSummary: The same rule applies in the reverse case: when the נכרי borrower converts, timing again decides whether the Jewish lender may collect the רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, a gentile borrowed money from a Jew with interest. The Jew added the interest onto the loan as part of the debt, and then the gentile converted. If it was added before he converted, the Jew collects the principal and also the interest. If it was added after he converted, he collects the principal but not the interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the mirror case, where now the borrower is the נכרי who converts and the lender is the Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew is allowed to charge a נכרי interest, so the loan started out permitted. If the interest was folded into the principal before the borrower converted, it is now just part of the debt and can be collected. If it was folded in only after he became a Jew, it is still interest owed by one Jew to another, so it cannot be collected.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly, the same rule applies to the next case
Before, while not yet
From when he converted, after the conversion

steps.whatToRemember: In both directions the rule is the same. Interest folded into the principal before the conversion is collected in full. Interest folded in after the conversion is not collected, and only the principal is paid.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן נׇכְרִי שֶׁלָּוָה מָעוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּרִבִּית
phrases.english: And similarly, a gentile who borrowed money from a Jew with interest
and he set it against him as a loan, and he converted,
phrases.notes: This time the Jewish lender does the rolling over, and the gentile borrower is the one who converts.

phrases.english: if before he converted
he set it against him as a loan,

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹבֶה אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וְגוֹבֶה אֶת הָרִבִּית.
phrases.english: he collects the principal and he collects the interest.
If after he converted
he set it against him as a loan,

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹבֶה אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וְאֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה אֶת הָרִבִּית.
phrases.english: he collects the principal but does not collect the interest.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן נׇכְרִי שֶׁלָּוָה מָעוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּרִבִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same rule from Step 3 to the reverse case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a נכרי borrower converts, the Jewish lender collects the רבית only if it was folded into the principal before the conversion. Otherwise he collects only the principal.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: The lender always collects both principal and interest
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rules that when a נכרי borrows from a Jew with רבית and then converts, the lender collects both the קרן and the רבית no matter when the debt was set.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: If a gentile borrowed money from a Jew with interest, either way, the lender collects the principal and also collects the interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a different opinion. רבי יוסי says the timing does not matter, and the Jewish lender collects everything from the convert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4, the first opinion said timing decides: only if the רבית was folded into the loan before the conversion may the lender collect it. רבי יוסי disagrees and lets the lender collect the רבית in every case, even though the borrower is now Jewish.

keyTerms.meaning: Either way; no matter which case
He collects (payment)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
A gentile who borrowed money from a Jew with interest,
whether this way or that way —
phrases.notes: He means: whether the interest was added into the loan before the conversion or after it.

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹבֶה אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וְגוֹבֶה אֶת הָרִבִּית.
phrases.english: he collects the principal and he collects the interest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a dissenting view to the timing rule in Step 4, saying timing does not matter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a נכרי borrower converts, the Jewish lender always collects both the קרן and the רבית.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of אמוראים, the גמרא rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said that רב חסדא said that רב הונא said: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling: we follow רבי יוסי, so the lender collects everything from the convert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling settles the disagreement in the ברייתא. The timing rule from Steps 3 and 4 is not the final הלכה for the case where the borrower converts.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows this opinion

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Chisda said that Rav Huna said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the law in favor of the opinion given in Step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, a lender collects both the קרן and the רבית from a borrower who converted.

steps.title: רבא asks for רבי יוסי's reason
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why רבי יוסי lets a Jew collect רבית from someone who is now a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the reason of רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a question that sets up his own explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking רבית from a fellow Jew is normally forbidden, so רבי יוסי's ruling needs a reason. רבא is asking what that reason is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling just accepted as הלכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוסי allows collecting רבית from a borrower who is now Jewish.

steps.title: So no one says he converted to escape his debts
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the rule protects the convert's reputation: otherwise people would say he converted to get out of paying the רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that people should not say: "This one converted for the sake of his money."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question. The lender collects so that people will not suspect the גר of converting just to save money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If conversion cancelled the רבית, people could think the borrower converted only to escape his debt. Making him pay in full removes that suspicion, so everyone can see the conversion was sincere.

keyTerms.meaning: So that people should not say
His money
He converted

steps.whatToRemember: The convert pays the רבית so his conversion will not look like a trick to escape his debt.

phrases.english: So that people should not say:
"This one converted for the sake of his money."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule prevents people from suspecting that the borrower converted only to avoid paying the רבית.

steps.title: A loan document with interest written in it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי מאיר says a lender whose loan document includes רבית is fined and collects nothing. The חכמים say he collects the קרן but not the רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A loan document in which interest is written: we fine him, and he collects neither the principal nor the interest. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The Sages say: He collects the principal but not the interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a loan document (שטר) that openly includes רבית. רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree about whether the lender can still collect the קרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that the lender cannot collect the רבית. The question is whether we also fine him by taking away the קרן, the money he really did lend.

keyTerms.meaning: A written loan document
We fine or penalize
The majority of the Sages

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A loan document in which interest is written —
we fine him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the lender, who wrote the forbidden interest into the document.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה לֹא אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וְלֹא אֶת הָרִבִּית,
phrases.english: and he collects neither the principal nor the interest,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹבֶה אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וְאֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה אֶת הָרִבִּית.
phrases.english: he collects the principal but does not collect the interest.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁטָר שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ רִבִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: fining a lender whose loan document includes רבית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: the lender loses both the קרן and the רבית. חכמים: he collects the קרן only.

steps.title: What is the basis of the disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the idea behind the disagreement. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides forbid the רבית. The גמרא wants to find the underlying principle that makes them differ about the קרן.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the principle behind the dispute in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that divides רבי מאיר and the חכמים.

steps.title: Do we fine the permitted part because of the forbidden part?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that we fine the permitted part (the קרן) because of the forbidden part (the רבית). The חכמים hold that we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: We fine the permitted part because of the forbidden part. And the Rabbis hold: We do not fine the permitted part because of the forbidden part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the disagreement. It is about whether a penalty can reach even the part of the loan that was perfectly fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרן is permitted because it is real money that was really lent. The רבית is forbidden. רבי מאיר takes away both as a penalty, while the חכמים take away only the forbidden part.

keyTerms.meaning: We fine or penalize
The permitted part
The forbidden part

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר fines the permitted part because of the forbidden part; the חכמים do not. Remember this, because the next case depends on it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
We fine the permitted part because of the forbidden part,
phrases.notes: The permitted part is the principal he really lent; the forbidden part is the interest.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold:
We do not fine the permitted part because of the forbidden part.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: קָנְסִינַן הֶתֵּירָא מִשּׁוּם אִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 by naming the principle in dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether we fine the permitted part (the קרן) because of the forbidden part (the רבית).

steps.title: Early-dated loan documents are invalid
steps.stepSummary: A משנה elsewhere rules that loan documents dated earlier than the real loan are invalid, while ones dated later are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: Loan documents that are dated early are invalid, and those dated late are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from another place about loan documents with a wrong date. This sets up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An early date is a problem because the document seems to give the lender rights from before the loan really happened. A later date only hurts the lender himself, so that document stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Loan documents
Dated earlier than the real loan
Dated later than the real loan

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in שביעית 10:5.

phrases.english: Loan documents that are dated early are invalid,
and those dated late are valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source that will be linked to the principle of Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Early-dated loan documents are invalid; late-dated ones are valid.

steps.title: Why not collect from the real date?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: even if the early date can't be used, the lender should still collect from the real date of the loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are early-dated documents invalid? Granted they can't collect from the first date, but let them collect from the second date!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. Throwing out the whole document seems too harsh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The false early date should not count. But the loan did really happen on the second, true date, so the document should at least work from that date.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Granted that
The first (false, written) date / the second (real) date

phrases.english: Why are early-dated documents invalid?
Granted they can't collect from the first date,
phrases.notes: The first date is the false, earlier date written on the document.

phrases.english: let them collect from the second date!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the משנה in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that early-dated documents are completely invalid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the false date is a problem; the real loan date should still allow the lender to collect.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: The משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the משנה is part of a dispute and follows רבי מאיר, who fines the permitted part because of the forbidden part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: It is taught as part of a dispute, and it is רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the challenge by linking the משנה to רבי מאיר from the earlier ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר fines the permitted part because of the forbidden part. Here the wrong date is the forbidden part, so the lender is fined by losing even his right to collect from the real date.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught as part of a dispute (it follows only one side)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
It is taught as part of a dispute,
and it is Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13 using the principle from Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to one side of a dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to follow everyone, which makes the full invalidation hard to understand.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who fines the lender even on the valid part because of the wrong date.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Even the חכמים agree, because of a גזירה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה can follow even the חכמים: the document is invalidated as a גזירה, so the lender won't come to collect from the false early date.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: You can even say it is the Rabbis — it is a decree, lest he collect from the first date.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer. The משנה need not follow only רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is not a fine. It is a safeguard: if the document stayed valid, the lender might use it to collect from the false early date. So the חכמים also invalidate it completely.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say
A rabbinic safeguard decree
Lest; out of concern that

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש: early-dated documents are invalid as a fine (רבי מאיר). רבי יוחנן: they are invalid as a גזירה, which even the חכמים accept.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן's reason is not a fine. He agrees the חכמים don't fine the permitted part; the invalidation is a safeguard against misuse of the false date.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
You can even say it is the Rabbis —
it is a decree, lest he collect from the first date.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: דחיה (of ריש לקיש's need to assign the משנה to רבי מאיר)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from ריש לקיש's to the challenge of Step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Invalidating the whole document seemed possible only as a fine, which would match רבי מאיר alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the חכמים invalidate it, so the lender will not come to collect from the false early date.

steps.title: A lender threatens to claim a mortgaged orchard as his own
steps.stepSummary: A man mortgaged his orchard. The lender ate its fruit for three years. Then the lender threatened to hide the mortgage document and claim he had bought the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man gave his orchard to his friend as security for a loan. The lender ate the fruit for three years. Then he told the owner: 'Sell it to me, good. If not, I will hide the mortgage document and say I bought it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story (a מעשה) about an orchard used as security for a loan. This sets up the case the גמרא will discuss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender is threatening a trick. After three years of using a field, a person can claim he owns it. So if the mortgage document disappears, the lender could falsely say he bought the field.

keyTerms.meaning: Gave as security (mortgaged) for a loan
An orchard
A mortgage document showing the field is only held as security
'It is bought, in my hands', a claim of ownership

phrases.english: A certain man who mortgaged
an orchard to his fellow,
he (the lender) ate its fruit for three years.
phrases.notes: Three years matters because using a field for three years lets a person claim he owns it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי מְזַבְּינַתְּ לַהּ נִיהֲלִי – מוּטָב,
phrases.english: He said to him: If you sell it to me – good,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא – כָּבֵישְׁנָא לַהּ לִשְׁטַר מַשְׁכַּנְתָּא
phrases.english: and if not – I will hide the mortgage document
and I will say: 'It is bought, it is in my hands.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּמַשְׁכֵּין לֵיהּ פַּרְדֵּיסָא לְחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case about mortgages and sales, separate from the earlier discussion of early-dated documents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the facts: a lender who held a mortgaged orchard for three years threatens to falsely claim he bought it.

steps.title: The borrower gives the field to his minor son, then sells it
steps.stepSummary: To protect himself, the borrower gave the field to his young son. After that he 'sold' it to the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and gave the field to his minor son. Then he sold it to the lender.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. The borrower uses a counter-trick: he gives the field away first, so the sale he makes afterward is worthless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the field belongs to the son, the father no longer owns it. So when the father 'sells' it to the lender, he is selling something that is not his. This lets him undo the forced sale later.

keyTerms.meaning: He transferred ownership of it
His minor (young) son
He sold it

phrases.english: He went and transferred it to his minor son,
and then sold it to him (the lender).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the facts of the story begun in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The borrower first gave the field to his minor son and then sold it to the lender, so the sale was of land he did not own.

steps.title: The sale is void, but how is the money collected?
steps.stepSummary: The sale is clearly not valid. The question is whether the buyer's money counts as a loan with a document, which can be collected from sold property, or an oral loan, which cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sale is certainly not a sale. Is the money like a loan with a document, so he can collect from property that was sold to others? Or is it like an oral loan, so he cannot?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states that the sale is void. Then it asks a real question about how the lender gets back the money he paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the sale fails, because the seller did not own the field. The doubt is only about the money. A loan with a שטר is publicly known, so it can be collected even from land the borrower later sold. An oral loan is not publicly known, so it cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: The money (coins) that was paid
A loan written in a document
An oral loan, with no document
Property tied to a debt that was since sold to others

steps.confusionAlert: The question is NOT whether the sale works. The גמרא already says it does not. The question is only about how the paid money can be collected.

phrases.english: The sale is certainly not a sale.
Is the money like a loan with a document
so he can collect from property that was sold,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא כְּמִלְוֶה עַל פֶּה דָּמוּ
phrases.english: or perhaps it is like an oral loan
so he cannot collect from property that was sold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the legal question that comes out of the story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the money paid for a void sale collected like a loan with a document, which reaches sold property, or like an oral loan, which does not?
steps.whyThisMatters: It decides whether the buyer can take back his money from people who later bought the seller's land.

steps.title: אביי links the question to רבי אסי
steps.stepSummary: אביי says this question is really the same as one already raised by רבי אסי, and begins to quote him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Isn't this the same as the question of רבי אסי? For רבי אסי said:
steps.whatsHappening: אביי points out that this issue is the same as something רבי אסי already said. The גמרא is setting up a quote, and his words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of answering directly, אביי says the question is not new. It matches what רבי אסי already said. If the two are really the same, whatever applies to רבי אסי's statement will apply here too.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't this the same as...?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וְלָאו הַיְינוּ דְּרַבִּי אַסִּי,
phrases.english: Abaye said: Isn't this the same as that of Rabbi Asi?
For Rabbi Asi said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question in step 18 by matching it to an earlier question by רבי אסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי says the question about the money in a void sale is the same as what רבי אסי said, which is quoted next.
